A faithful **process-bigraph port** of the archived
[`vivarium-collective/island-biogeography`](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/island-biogeography)
Lotka-Volterra metacommunity model. Each island is a time-stepped
`Process`; a single migration coupler exchanges individuals between islands by
distance. The port reproduces the reference's discrete population dynamics
exactly (not a paraphrase), decomposed into composable process-bigraph parts so
an archipelago is a real composite: *N* island processes + 1 migration coupler.

## What it wraps

The reference model (`experiments/island_lotka_volterra.py`,
`experiments/island_food_web.py`) simulates a set of islands, each holding a
per-species abundance dict, a carrying capacity derived from island area, a
Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix, and a mean growth rate. Each generation every
island applies a discrete LV step, individuals migrate between islands with a
distance-decaying probability, and new species are occasionally introduced.

This package ports that model into:

| Class | Role | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `IslandProcess` | One island's discrete Lotka-Volterra step (+ carrying-capacity rescale and per-island random introduction) | `Island.update_populations` |
| `MigrationProcess` | Distance-stochastic single-individual migration coupling every island pair (`rate = 1/(1+distance)`) | `IslandManager.simulate` |

and two `@composite_generator`s:

| Generator | Interaction structure |
|---|---|
| `island_archipelago` | random interaction matrix |
| `island_food_web` | antisymmetric predator-prey matrix from a generated trophic food web |

## Installation

```bash
# From PyPI (once published):
pip install viva-island-biogeography
# or with uv:
uv pip install viva-island-biogeography

# For development (editable):
uv venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

> Once installed, the processes register automatically via
> `bigraph_schema.package.discover` — no manual `register_link()` calls are
> needed. The workspace also ships `viva_island_biogeography.core.build_core()`,
> which registers the processes explicitly for runners/dashboards that build
> their own core.

## Quick start

```python
from process_bigraph import Composite, gather_emitter_results
from viva_island_biogeography.core import build_core
from viva_island_biogeography.composites.archipelago import island_archipelago

core = build_core()
doc = island_archipelago(core, n_islands=4, n_species=30, seed=0)
sim = Composite({"state": doc}, core=core)
sim.run(100.0)                      # 100 generations
rows = gather_emitter_results(sim)[("emitter",)]
last = rows[-1]["islands"]          # {island_name: {species: count}}
```

## API reference

### `IslandProcess`

| Port | Dir | Schema | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `abundance` | in/out | `map[string,float]` | per-species counts (read in; **delta** out) |
| `immigration` | in | `map[string,float]` | external arrivals a sibling may inject |
| `growth_modifier` | in | `float` | environmental multiplier on growth (default 1.0) |
| `richness` | out | `float` | local species-richness readout (delta) |

Key config: `species_list`, `interaction_matrix`, `mean_growth_rate`, `area`,
`individuals_per_area`, `introduction_probability`, `x`, `y`, `seed`.

### `MigrationProcess`

| Port | Dir | Schema | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `abundances` | in | `map[string,map[string,float]]` | all islands' abundance maps |
| `exchange` | out | `map[string,map[string,float]]` | per-island per-species migration deltas |

Config: `island_names`, `positions`, `seed`.

## Architecture

Abundances live in a shared `islands` store (`{island: {species: count}}`). Each
`IslandProcess` emits an abundance **delta** so the engine accumulates
contributions additively; the `MigrationProcess` emits its migration deltas to
the same store. Both read the pre-tick state and their deltas sum, reproducing
the reference's `LV -> migration -> introduction` net effect per generation. A
RAM emitter captures the abundance tree, a richness readout, and time.

## Showcase investigation

The `island-biogeography` investigation
(`workspace/investigations/island-biogeography/`) binds three studies that test
the model against MacArthur-Wilson island-biogeography theory:

<!-- BEGIN:investigations -->
<!-- generated by `vivarium-workbench gen-readme` — edit the source, not this table -->

| Investigation | Research question |
|---|---|
| [Island biogeography: a Lotka-Volterra metacommunity under contract _(running)_](https://vivarium-collective.github.io/viva-island-biogeography/investigations/island-biogeography.html) | Does the archived island-biogeography Lotka-Volterra metacommunity model, faithfully ported into process-bigraph, reproduce the two central predictions of MacArthur-Wilson island biogeography — speci… |
<!-- END:investigations -->

| Study | Claim | Headline result |
|---|---|---|
| `island-archipelago` | area sets abundance, not richness | `corr(total, area) ~ 1.0`; `corr(richness, log area) ~ -0.1` |
| `distance-immigration` | isolation reduces colonization; migration conserves individuals | `corr(immigration, distance) ~ -0.7`; net flux `= 0` |
| `island-food-web` | trophic structure restores the species-area law | `corr(richness, log area) ~ +0.5`; `+1.8` species vs random |

Run a study locally (from the workspace root):

```bash
python workspace/studies/island-archipelago/sims/run.py
```

Each runner builds the composite, computes the behavior-test scalars, renders
interactive Plotly visualizations into `workspace/studies/<slug>/viz/`, and
records the run to `.pbg/runs.jsonl`.

### Expected outputs (behavior-test verdicts)

All six behavior tests pass against the measured ensemble values:

- `abundance-scales-with-area` — `capacity_area_corr > 0.95` (measured ~1.00)
- `richness-not-set-by-area` — `richness_area_corr < 0.35` (measured ~-0.10)
- `isolation-reduces-immigration` — `immigration_distance_corr < -0.3` (measured ~-0.7)
- `migration-conserves-individuals` — `|total_net_migration| < 1e-9` (exactly 0)
- `food-web-recovers-species-area` — `richness_area_corr > 0.2` (measured ~+0.50)
- `trophic-coexistence-exceeds-random` — `richness_gain_over_random > 0.5` (measured ~+1.8)

## Limitations and assumptions

- **Discrete-time model.** One composite tick is one generation; the `interval`
  magnitude is not sub-divided.
- **Synchronous composition nuance.** Within a tick, migration reads pre-LV
  counts, so single-individual abundance undershoots of magnitude ≤1 can occur
  transiently and self-heal the next generation (see the `MigrationProcess`
  docstring). The `MigrationProcess` itself never over-emigrates (it decrements
  a working copy) and conserves individuals exactly.
- **Richness is low and noisy** because Lotka-Volterra competition drives strong
  exclusion; the species-area and distance results are ensemble means over seeds.
- This is a stylised ecological model, not a calibrated empirical one; the
  thresholds are theory/calibration anchors, not fits to field data.
